key_insight: Experimentally trained surrogate models can forecast cylinder-wake dynamics quickly, but accuracy degrades as transient, high-frequency flow features become harder to infer from imperfect measurements.
engineering_relevance: These models could enable faster-than-real-time flow prediction for control and monitoring, especially when only limited experimental data are available.
method: Train fully convolutional neural networks, U-Nets, Fourier neural operators, and DMD-based models on PIV velocity fields.
Evaluate short- and long-horizon forecasting at fixed Re = 590.
Test robustness across a broader Reynolds-number range (Re = 230 to 2920) with noisy and incomplete observations.
evidence_signal: On two-dimensional, two-component PIV data, the models produced meaningful short-term forecasts and propagated low-frequency dynamics, but struggled to preserve transient features and high-frequency energy over longer horizons.
watch_item: Performance may drop sharply when measurements are noisy, incomplete, or increasingly three-dimensional, so deployment will require careful sensing and validation.
paper_title: Data-driven surrogate models for forecasting experimentally measured fluid flows
